Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כל היכא דתני הכל, כולהו מייתי להו בשמעתא קמייתא דערכין, ומפרש הכל לאתויי מאי. והכל שוחטין דמתניתין פליגי בה אמוראי בגמרא, למר לאתויי טמא בחולין, ולמר לאתויי כותי או מומר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: All may slaughter - Wherever [a Mishnah] teaches the word "all" (hakol), all such instances are gathered together in the first passage of tractate Arachin, where it explains, for each one, what "all" comes to include. And as for "all may slaughter" in our Mishnah, the Amoraim disagree about it in the Gemara: according to one, it comes to include a tamei person [slaughtering] non-sacred [animals]; and according to another, it comes to include a Samaritan (Kuti) or an apostate (mumar).

Rashi on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: And all of them - The Gemara explains what [the phrase] "and all of them" comes to include.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.hebrew: ושחיטתן כשרה דיעבד - בתמיה. וקשה, רישא דמשמע דההוא דאתרבי מהכל לכתחלה אתרבי, ואילו סיפא משמע דכי מרבינן מהכל דיעבד מרבינן לה, אבל לכתחלה לא אתרבי. והא ליכא למימר כולה מתניתין לכתחלה וחדא קתני, דכיון דתנא הכל שוחטין פשיטא דכשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:2:1.english: And their slaughter is valid after the fact - This is said as a question. And it is difficult: the first clause implies that that which is included by [the word] "all" was included [as valid] ab initio, whereas the last clause implies that when we include [something] from [the word] "all," we include it [only as valid] after the fact, but it was not included [as valid] ab initio. And one cannot say that the entire Mishnah speaks of [validity] ab initio and is teaching a single [uniform] point, because since it taught "all may slaughter," it is obvious that [the slaughter] is valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.hebrew: וכל הכל לכתחלה הוא - דתקשה לך, ולא תוכל לומר כולה דיעבד, וה"ק: הכל תורת שחיטה נוהגת בהן, שאם שחטו אותן הפסולין דמתרבי, תהא שחיטתן כשרה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:1.english: And does every [use of the word] "all" indicate that it is permitted ab initio? - For [otherwise] it would be difficult for you, and you could not say that the entire [phrase "all may slaughter"] refers to validity after the fact; rather, this is what it means: the law of [valid] slaughter fully applies to them, so that if these disqualified people who are included by [the word] "all" performed slaughter, their slaughter would be valid.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.hebrew: אלא הכל ממירים - מי מצית למימר לכתחלה יביא בהמת חולין אצל בהמת קדשים ויאמר זו תמורת זו? הכל דתמורה מפרש התם לאתויי יורש שממיר בקרבן אביו לאחר מיתת אביו, דהתם תנן אין ממירין בשל אחרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:2.english: Rather, all may effect temurah - Could you possibly say that one may, from the outset (lechatchilah), bring a non-sacred (chullin) animal next to a consecrated (kodashim) animal and say, "This one is a substitute (temurah) for that one"? [Rather,] the word "all" with regard to temurah is expounded there [in tractate Temurah] to include an heir who effects temurah on his father's offering after his father's death - for there we learned: one may not effect temurah with an animal belonging to others.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:3:4.english: Bad - [meaning] an animal with a blemish.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - דעקר להכל דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא, אבל הכל שוחטין בדוכתיה קאי, דכל כמה דלא עקר ליה. ותנא לא שיהו הפסולים רשאים לשחוט כדעקר התם, משמע דלכתחלה רבינהו, והדר תני ושחיטתן כשרה, דמשמע דיעבד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, since it taught the reason - [This continuation of the Mishnah, in Temurah,] negates the ["all"] of the first clause, so that you should not say it means [that substitution is permitted] ab initio. But "all may slaughter" [in our Mishnah] stands as it is, since as long as [the Mishnah] has not negated it - and the Tanna did not teach [a qualifier] such as "not that the disqualified are permitted to slaughter," the way it negated it there [in Temurah] - this implies that it included them ab initio. And it then teaches "and their slaughter is valid," which implies [that this validity applies only] after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: לא שהאדם רשאי - דכתיב "לא יחליפנו", ורישא הכי קאמר: הכל דין תמורה נוהגת בהם. והא דתנא ברישא "הכל ממירין" ואיצטריך ליה תו לפרושי "לא שהאדם רשאי" כו', ולא נקט ברישא לשון קצרה "הכל שהמירו תמורתם תמורה" - לשון התנאים הוא זה, כמו "הכל שוחטין", "הכל סומכין", "הכל חייבין", הלכך הכא אע"ג דהוצרך להאריך לא שינה התנא את לשונו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: Not that a person is permitted - since it is written, "he shall not exchange it" [referring to a consecrated animal], and the opening statement [of the Mishnah] means to say this: the law of substitution (temurah) applies to them. And as for the fact that it taught at the outset "everyone may effect a substitution," and it then needed to further explain "not that a person is permitted [to do so]..." etc. - and did not instead use at the outset the shorter formulation "whoever exchanged [a consecrated animal], their substitution is valid" - this is because [the phrase] "everyone..." is the standard language of the Tannaim, like "all may slaughter," "all may perform semikhah," "all are obligated." Therefore here, even though it needed to elaborate further, the Tanna did not change his customary language.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:3.english: Substitution takes effect [mumar] - [meaning] the second animal becomes consecrated [along with the first], and both of them are sacred.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:4:4.english: And he receives forty lashes - because of the prohibition, "He shall not exchange it" (lo yamir).

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.hebrew: הכל מעריכין - התם מפרש לאתויי מופלא סמוך לאיש, קטן היודע להפלות לשם מי מקדישין, ואם סמוך לפרקו הוא, כגון בן י"ב שנה ויום אחד, דבריו קיימין, אע"פ שעדיין קטן הוא עד י"ג שנה ויום אחד:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:1.english: All may valuate [themselves] - There [in tractate Arachin] it explains that [the word] "all" comes to include a mufla samukh le'ish (a minor approaching manhood) - a minor who knows how to distinguish [the concept of] to whom [something] is consecrated. And if he is close to his age of majority, such as one who is twelve years and one day old, his words are valid, even though he is still legally a minor until thirteen years and one day.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.hebrew: מעריכין - תורת מעריכין עליהם, שאם אמר ערכי עלי או ערך פלוני עלי, נדרו קיים, ואע"ג דקטן הוא זה הנודר, חייב ליתן כפי שנים של נערך, והדמים קצובין בפרשה:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:2.english: They may vow valuations (ma'arichin) - The law of valuation-vows applies to them, such that if one said, "My valuation is incumbent upon me," or, "The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me," his vow is valid. And even though this vower is a minor, he is obligated to pay according to the years of the one being valued, the sums being fixed in the Torah portion [Leviticus 27].

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.hebrew: הכל נערכין - יש להם ערך, ואפילו מוכה שחין שאינו שוה כלום לימכר בשוק, יש לו ערך הכתוב בפרשה. ואם אמר על עצמו ערכי עלי, או אמר על אחר ערך מוכה שחין זה עלי, לא אמרינן הואיל ודמים אין לו ערך נמי אין לו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:3.english: All are subject to valuation - They have a [fixed] valuation; and even someone afflicted with boils, who is worth nothing to be sold in the market [as a slave], has the valuation written in the Torah portion. And if one said about himself, "my valuation is upon me," or said about another, "the valuation of this person afflicted with boils is upon me," we do not say: since he has no [market] worth, he likewise has no valuation.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.hebrew: הכל נודרים - דמי עלי או דמי פלוני עלי. והתם מפרש, דאיידי דבעי למיתני הכל נידרין, תנא נמי הכל נודרים:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:4.english: All may vow [a person's worth] - [That is, one may say,] "my worth is incumbent upon me" or "so-and-so's worth is incumbent upon me." And there [in tractate Arachin], it explains that since it needed to teach "all may be the subject of such a vow" (hakol nidarin), it also taught "all may make such a vow" (hakol nodarim).

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.hebrew: הכל נידרים - כל אדם השוה כלום, יש לו דמים. ואם אמר דמי עלי, או אמר על אחר דמי פלוני עלי, נותן לפי מה שהוא נמכר בשוק. ואפילו היה הנידר זה פחות מבן חדש, ואמר דמי תינוק זה עלי, יתן דמיו, ואע"פ שאין פחות מבן חדש נערך. ואם אמר ערכו עלי, פטור מכלום, שלא נתנה בו תורה ערך, דכתיב (ויקרא כז) ואם מבן חדש ועד בן חמש שנים, דמים מיהא יש לו לפי שויו, ואם אמר בתורת דמים, נותן דמיו:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:5.english: All are vowed - Any person who is worth something has a monetary value (damim). And if he says, "My value (dami) is upon me," or says of another, "The value (dami) of so-and-so is upon me," he pays according to what that person would sell for in the marketplace. And even if the one vowed was less than a month old, and he said, "The value (dami) of this infant is upon me," he must give his [market] value, even though a child less than a month old is not subject to a fixed Torah valuation (erech). But if he said, "His erech is upon me," he is exempt from paying anything, since the Torah did not assign him a fixed valuation, as it is written (Vayikra 27), "And if from a month old to five years old" [implying that below a month there is no fixed valuation]. He does, however, have a market value (damim), according to his worth - and if he said, "in terms of damim," he pays his [market] value.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:5:6.english: There shall be no sin in you - This implies: but if you do vow, there will be sin in you.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.hebrew: טוב אשר לא תדור - לעיל מיניה כתיב את אשר תדור שלם, ואפילו הכי טוב אשר לא תדור, שמא תדור ולא תשלם. הכי מפרש ליה רבי מאיר:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: Better that you should not vow - Above this [verse in Kohelet] it is written, "That which you vow, pay" (Kohelet 5:3), and even so, [it also says] "Better that you should not vow" - lest you vow and not pay. This is how Rabbi Meir explains it.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה - מנודר ומשלם, ומנודר ואינו משלם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than this and than that - [better] than one who vows and pays, and [better] than one who vows and does not pay.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:3.english: One who does not vow at all - For one who is accustomed to making vows will eventually come to violate [the prohibition], "he shall not break his word."

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר טוב מזה ומזה נודר ומשלם - דהכי משמע, טוב אשר לא תדור משתדור ולא תשלם, אבל משתדור ותשלם לא, שהוא טוב מכולם:
Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:4.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Better than either of these is one who vows and pays - For this is the implication [of the verse]: "Better is one who does not vow" than one who vows and does not pay, but not [better] than one who vows and pays - for that [vowing and paying] is better than all of them.

Rashi on Chullin 2a:6:5.english: And even R' Yehuda states this only when he says, "This is [designated]" - for if it died or was stolen, he is not liable for its guarantee [to bring another in its place]. Alternatively, since he has [already] set it aside [as consecrated], he can no longer retract from it.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל שוחטין - כתוב בהלכות ארץ ישראל דנשים לא ישחטו, מפני שדעתן קלות. ואין נראה, דאפילו במוקדשין שוחטות לכתחלה, כדאמרינן פרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:): כל הפסולים ששחטו, דיעבד אין, לכתחלה לא. ורמינהי: "ושחט" - מלמד שהשחיטה כשרה כו'. ומשני: הוא הדין דאפילו לכתחלה, אלא משום דבעי למיתני טמא במוקדשים דלכתחלה לא, תנא נמי "ששחטו". ולא קאמר משום דבעי למיתני נשים דתנא להו ברישא, אלא ודאי משום דנשים שוחטות לכתחלה אפילו במוקדשין. והא דלא קתני "הכל שוחטין אחד אנשים ואחד נשים" כדקתני בתמורה (דף ב.), התם אצטריך למיתנייה כדפירש בריש תמורה, משום דכל הפרשה כולה נאמרה בלשון זכר, אבל הכא אין חידוש באשה יותר מבאיש. ובפרק כל הפסולין (זבחים דף לא:) גבי קדשים איצטריך למיתני נשים, משום דבשאר עבודות נשים פסולות אפילו כהנות:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:1.english: All may slaughter - It is written in Hilchot Eretz Yisrael that women should not slaughter, because their minds are flighty. But this does not seem [correct], for even with consecrated animals they may slaughter ab initio, as we say in the chapter Kol HaPesulin (Zevachim 31b): all those disqualified [from the Temple service] who slaughtered - after the fact, yes; ab initio, no. And we raise a contradiction: "and he shall slaughter" teaches that the slaughtering is valid, etc. And it answers: the same is true even ab initio, but because it wanted to teach [the case of] a tamei person with consecrated animals, that ab initio it is not [permitted], it therefore also used the wording "who slaughtered" [i.e., after the fact]. And it did not say that [the reason for this wording] is because it wanted to teach about women, whom it had already taught in the first clause - but rather, certainly, because women may slaughter ab initio even with consecrated animals. And as for the fact that it does not teach "all may slaughter, both men and women," as it teaches in Temurah (2a) - there it was necessary to teach it, as is explained at the beginning of Temurah, because that entire passage is stated in the masculine; but here there is no more novelty in [including] a woman than a man. And in the chapter Kol HaPesulin (Zevachim 31b), regarding consecrated items, it was necessary to teach [explicitly] "women," because with regard to other sacrificial services women are disqualified, even if they are daughters of priests.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.hebrew: שמא יקלקלו כו' - בגמרא (לקמן חולין יב:) דייק מדקתני "שמא יקלקלו" ולא קתני "שמא קלקלו", ש"מ אין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה. ופ"ה: אפילו אחרים רואין אותן. וק' לפירושו, דהא מסיפא שמעינן לה: "וכולן ששחטו ואחרים רואין אותן" כו', דמשמע דיעבד דוקא. וליכא למימר דדיעבד נקט משום טמא במוקדשין או אין מומחין, אבל חש"ו אפילו לכתחלה שוחטין באחרים רואין אותן, דהא רבא הוא דדייק "שמא קלקלו" לא קתני, ולרבא לא קאי "וכולן ששחטו" אלא אחש"ו, כדאמרינן בגמרא. וי"מ דגרס לקמן "רבה", אבל רבא לא דייק בין "יקלקלו" ל"קלקלו", כי היכי דלא חייש בהא דלא קתני "ואם שחטו". ור"ת מפרש, דאין מוסרין להן חולין לכתחלה לשחוט, אפילו כדי להשליך לכלבים, דלמא אתי למיכל, שיטעו להכשיר שחיטתן מתוך שיראו שמוסרים להן, כדפטר לקמן שחיטתן מכסוי, דלמא אתי למימר שחיטה מעלייתא היא. וניחא השתא, דבאין אחרים רואין אותן עסקינן ברישא:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:1:2.english: Lest they render it unfit, etc. - In the Gemara (below, Chullin 12b), it is inferred from the fact that it teaches "lest they render it unfit" and does not teach "lest they rendered it unfit," that non-sacred animals are not entrusted to them [a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor] to slaughter ab initio. And Rashi explains: this is so even when others are watching them. And this is difficult for his interpretation, for we could already derive this from the latter clause: "and all of them, if they slaughtered, with others watching them," etc. - which implies that it is specifically after the fact [that this is valid, but not ab initio]. And one cannot say that it stated "after the fact" only on account of a tamei person with consecrated items, or judges who are not experts, but that a deaf-mute, imbecile, or minor may in fact slaughter even ab initio when others are watching them - for it is Rava who infers this from the fact that "lest they rendered it unfit" is not taught, and according to Rava, "and all of them who slaughtered" refers not to the tamei person or the non-experts but to the deaf-mute, imbecile, and minor, as we say in the Gemara. And some explain that the text further on reads "Rabbah" [as the one who makes that inference], while Rava does not distinguish between "they will render it unfit" and "they rendered it unfit" - just as he is not troubled by the fact that it does not teach elsewhere "and if they slaughtered." And Rabbeinu Tam explains that non-sacred animals are not entrusted to them to slaughter ab initio even in order to throw the meat to dogs, lest others come to eat from it - that is, lest people mistakenly validate their slaughter upon seeing that these animals are entrusted to them, just as, further on, their slaughter is exempted from the obligation of covering the blood, lest one come to say it is a proper act of slaughter. And it fits well now, with this, that the first clause deals with a case where others are not watching them.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא - פירש בקונטרס, דעקר ליה להכל דרישא, דלא תימא לכתחלה הוא. ולשון "כדקתני טעמא" לא משמע כפירושו. ומה שפירש נמי במסקנא, גבי "דאי דיעבד תרתי דיעבד למה לי" - ואע"ג דבתמורה נמי תני והדר מפרש, התם לא תנא כי האי גוונא "הכל ממירין ותמורתן תמורה" גבי הדדי. ואי משום "לא שהאדם רשאי להמיר" משום דבעי לאסוקי "וסופג את הארבעים" לאשמועינן דלוקין על לאו שאין בו מעשה - אין נראה, דמשום "וסופג את הארבעים" לחודיה לא הוה ליה למיתני תרתי דיעבד, דהוה מצי למיתני "הכל ממירים והממיר סופג את הארבעים". ועוד, דבריש תמורה (דף ב.) פריך: הכל ממירים לכתחלה, ולא שהאדם רשאי להמיר דיעבד? ומשני, התם רב יהודה: הכי קתני, הכל מתפיסים בתמורה, אחד שוגג ואחד מזיד. והוה ליה לשנויי דתנא ליה משום "וסופג את הארבעים", כדפירש בקונטרס כאן. ונראה לרבינו תם, דשינויא דהכא הוי כההיא דתמורה, והכי קאמר: "התם כדקתני טעמא" - דלהכי תנא "הכל ממירים" דמשמע לכתחלה, לאשמעינן שאפילו המיר במזיד, דהיינו לכתחלה, מומר, דלא תימא ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר, כדאמרן בהתודה (מנחות פא.). וקשה לפירושו, דבסוף פרק קמא דתמורה (דף יג.) משמע דמן הדין ראוי להיות תמורה במזיד יותר מבשוגג, דקאמר "יהיה" לרבות שוגג כמזיד. ויש לומר, דלענין בהמה שתהא כשרה למזבח, פשוט לן שוגג יותר ממזיד. אי נמי, התם איירי במזיד ולא אתרו ביה, דלא הוו ארבעים בכתפיה, וההוא מזיד פשוט לן יותר משוגג:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:1.english: There, since it teaches the reason - Rashi explains that this negates [the implication of] "all" in the first clause, so that you should not say that [effecting a temurah] is permitted ab initio. But the wording "since it teaches the reason" does not suggest his explanation. And what he explains as well in the conclusion, regarding [the question] "if it is [only valid] after the fact, why do I need it taught twice as being after the fact?" - [is also difficult]: even though in Temurah too it teaches [the law] and only afterward explains it, there it did not teach in this fashion, "all may effect a temurah, and their temurah is a valid temurah," together [in one clause]. And if [the reason for] "not that a person is permitted to effect a temurah" is that it wanted to go on to teach "and he receives forty lashes," in order to teach us that one is lashed for [transgressing] a prohibition that involves no action - this does not seem right, for on account of "and he receives forty lashes" alone it would not have needed to teach "after the fact" twice, since it could have taught simply, "all may effect a temurah, and one who effects a temurah receives forty lashes." Furthermore, at the beginning of Temurah (2a) it asks: does "all may effect a temurah" mean ab initio, and "not that a person is permitted to effect a temurah" mean after the fact? And it answers there, in the name of Rav Yehuda: this is what it teaches - all may bind an animal into temurah-status, whether unwittingly or intentionally. And it should have answered instead that this was taught on account of "and he receives forty lashes," as Rashi explained here. And it seems to Rabbeinu Tam that the answer here is like that answer in Temurah, and this is what it means: "there, since it teaches the reason" - it is for this reason that it taught "all may effect a temurah," which implies ab initio, to teach us that even one who effected a temurah intentionally - that is, ab initio - has created a valid temurah, so that you should not say: he merely receives forty lashes on his back while [the animal] remains an ordinary non-sacred animal [i.e., the temurah did not take effect] - as we said in [the chapter] "HaMitvadeh" (Menachot 81a). But this explanation is difficult, for at the end of the first chapter of Temurah (13a) it implies that, by strict law, a temurah ought more properly to take effect when done intentionally than when done unwittingly, since it says that [the word] "it shall be" comes to include an unwitting act just like an intentional one. And one can answer that with regard to the animal being fit for the altar, it is obvious to us [that this applies] to an unwitting act more than to an intentional one. Alternatively, there it is dealing with an intentional act for which he was not forewarned, so that there are no forty lashes on his back - and that kind of intentional act is obvious to us [as creating a temurah] more than an unwitting one.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.hebrew: וסופג את הארבעים - וא"ת: הוה ליה למימר "וסופג שמונים", דהא תרי לאוי כתיב, "לא יחליפנו" ו"לא ימיר". ויש לומר, דחד בשלו וחד בשל חברו, כדאמר בתמורה (דף ט.), וכגון דאמר חברו: "כל הרוצה להמיר בבהמתו ימיר", דבענין אחר אין ממירין בשל אחרים. והכי איתא בהדיא בתמורה פ"ק:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:4:2.english: And he receives the forty [lashes] - And if you say: it should have stated "and he receives eighty," for behold two prohibitions are written, "he shall not exchange it" and "he shall not substitute for it." One may answer: one [prohibition] applies to [substituting] one's own [animal], and the other applies to [substituting] another's, as is stated in [tractate] Temurah (9a) - namely, in a case where the other person had said, "whoever wishes to effect substitution with his animal may do so," for otherwise one cannot effect substitution with another's [animal]. And this is stated explicitly in the first chapter of Temurah.

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:1.hebrew: וכתיב טוב אשר לא תדור - מעיקרא מייתי מדברי תורה, והדר מייתי מדברי קבלה:
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:1.english: And it is written, "It is better that you should not vow" - At first it brings [a proof] from the words of the Torah, and then it brings [a proof] from the words of the Tradition (i.e., the Prophets and Writings).

Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.hebrew: טוב מזה ומזה שאינו נודר כל עיקר - פ"ה: דלעיל מיניה כתיב "את אשר תדור שלם", ואפילו הכי "טוב אשר לא תדור" - שמא תדור ולא תשלם. וקשה לר"ת, דלא מייתי בגמרא ההוא קרא כלל. ונראה לר"ת דכולי מלתא דריש מהאי קרא, דהוה ליה למיכתב "טוב אשר לא תדור משתדור", ואנא ידענא דמשתדור ולא תשלם קאמר, אלא להכי קאמר "ולא תשלם" לגלויי על "משתדור" דמשתדור כדרך הנודרין קאמר, שנודרין ומשלמין, כדאמר גבי שכיר ותושב "בא זה ולימד על זה" (קדושין דף ד.):
Tosafot on Chullin 2a:6:2.english: Better than either is one who does not vow at all - Rashi explains: the verse immediately preceding this one states, "That which you vow, pay it" [Kohelet 5:3], and nevertheless [the next verse continues], "It is better that you not vow" [Kohelet 5:4] - lest you vow and not pay. And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, since the Gemara does not cite that verse [Kohelet 5:3] at all. Rabbeinu Tam therefore holds that the entire matter is derived from this verse [Kohelet 5:4] alone: it should have written simply, "Better that you not vow than that you vow," and I would [already] know that it means "than that you vow and not pay" - rather, it specifically says "and not pay" in order to clarify [something] about [the phrase] "than that you vow": that "than that you vow" speaks of vowing in the ordinary manner of those who vow - that is, that they vow and [do] pay - just as is said regarding the hired worker and the resident alien, "this one comes and teaches about that one" (Kiddushin 4a).
